title: Policy-driven audit routing and signed manifests for customer-managed blob sinks
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Goal: Implement a policy-driven audit forwarding subsystem for Private/VPC/On-Prem deployments that supports customer-managed object stores (S3-compatible, GCS, Azure Blob) while providing cryptographic provenance (signed manifests), optional envelope encryption with customer keys, resumable uploads, and operator claimability for incident diagnostics. This ticket covers design and implementation of the routing policy engine, manifest signing protocol, upload orchestration, and controls required by RBAC v2 and admin workflows.
acceptance_criteria: Private/Raft nodes can register multiple customer sink connectors and attach a routing policy (by org, region, severity) that determines event partitions to forward.

For each forwarded batch, a signed manifest (COSE or similar) is generated including batch id, SHA256 of payload, originating instance id, timestamp, and KMS key id. Signatures verifiable by customers and by Redwood ops.

Support for envelope encryption where the audit payload is encrypted with a CEK, which is wrapped with customer-provided asymmetric key material (CMEK or customer-managed HSM). Integration tests for S3/GCS/Azure flows pass.
Upload orchestration supports resumable transfers (chunked + manifest references) and ensures at-least-once but idempotent storage semantics using manifest dedup keys.
Admin console exposes per-sink status, last-successful-offset, failure reason, and allows operators to trigger manual replays with appropriate RBAC v2 controls.
End-to-end telemetry captured in Console: per-batch latency, retry counts, failure taxonomy, and cost estimates for customer-sink egress, with sample dashboards.
Automated chaos tests for network partitions and customer-sink auth rotation demonstrate graceful backoff and safe buffering without data loss within configured retention windows.
Security review completed and design doc approved in Confluence.
implementation_plan: Design: complete signed-manifest format and fields; select canonical signature scheme (COSE/EDS) and canonical JSON/CBOR representation.
Platform: extend audit-forwarder to include routing policy engine and per-sink connector plugins (S3/GCS/Azure/HTTP).
Encryption: implement envelope encryption hook points; integrate with KMIP/HSM and cloud KMS for wrap/unwrap flows.
Resumable uploads: implement chunked upload protocol with manifest referencing and resume tokens; ensure idempotency keys.
RBAC/Console: add sink-level permissions (create/update/delete/trigger-replay/view-status) mapped to RBAC v2 roles; add console UI and API endpoints.
Tests: unit, integration with mocked clouds, e2e on a private cluster and airgapped testbed; chaos scenarios for auth rotation and network egress failures.
Docs & runbook: publish customer integration guide, admin troubleshooting runbook, and compliance checklist for regulated customers.
Rollout: staged rollout starting with internal beta customers -> limited customers on Dedicated -> general availability for Private with opt-in.
tradeoffs: Choosing stronger signature schemes (COSE/CMS) increases CPU at the forwarder; we favor a compact, well-understood scheme to balance performance and verifiability.
Resumable uploads require maintaining in-memory or lightweight on-disk state per active transfer; we accept additional storage overhead for reliability.
Envelope encryption with customer keys increases integration complexity and adds latency; we make it optional and recommend tenant-level configs.
Stricter at-most-once semantics would require synchronous handshakes and complex de-duplication; we implement idempotent manifests and at-least-once with dedup keys to simplify and be resilient.
qa_plan: Unit tests for manifest signing and verification across supported algorithms.
Integration tests against real S3-compatible test buckets, GCS emulator, and Azure Blob storage in CI.
E2E run on a Private deployment with a seeded workload to validate routing policies and performance targets.
Security fuzzing of manifest fields and verification paths; pen-test on KMS interactions.
Operational run: enable feature flag for one internal org for 2 weeks, monitor metrics and run manual replays.
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged rollout: internal-only for week 1 (on private cluster).
Dedicated customers opt-in period and remediation window (week 5-8).
GA release gated on stability, security sign-off, and docs completion (week 12).
